Definition: from G4012 and G2064 (including its alternate); to come all around, i.e. stroll, vacillate, veer:--fetch a compass, vagabond, wandering about.
BiblicalUsage: Perierchomai means to go about, to wander around. Paul warns that younger widows learn to be idle, wandering about from house to house as tattlers and busybodies, and certain vagabond Jews went about calling the name of Jesus over the demon-possessed.
TheologicalSignificance: I take it that going about is a gift when it serves and a snare when it idles: the same wandering can carry the gospel or carry gossip.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
